AES Text Encryptor

Encrypt text with real AES-256-GCM using a password-derived key (PBKDF2), fully in your browser.

AES Text Encryptor

Real AES-256-GCM encryption with a PBKDF2 password key. Nothing leaves your browser.

Output is Base64(salt 16B | IV 12B | ciphertext). PBKDF2: 100,000 iterations, SHA-256, AES-256-GCM.

📖 How to use

  1. Choose Encrypt or Decrypt mode.
  2. Enter a strong password (you will need it to decrypt).
  3. Paste your text (or the encrypted Base64 string) and click the button.
  4. Copy the result — the output packs salt, IV and ciphertext into one string.

❓ Frequently asked questions

Is this real encryption?

Yes. It uses WebCrypto PBKDF2 with 100,000 SHA-256 iterations and a random salt to derive an AES-256-GCM key — the same building blocks used by professional tools. The main weakness is a short, guessable password.

Why does encrypting the same text give different output?

Each encryption uses a fresh random salt and IV, so encrypting the same text twice produces different output. Both are needed to decrypt.

What if I forget the password?

No. Decryption fails and you get a clear error. There is no password recovery — keep your password safe.

Can I decrypt on another device?

The encrypted output is self-contained: salt, IV and ciphertext packed into one Base64 string, so it decrypts on any device with the password.
